scope: Bihar food heritage records relevant to Patna discovery and archival context

records.name: Litti Chokha
records.claim: Bihar Tourism identifies litti as a Bihari main-course dish made from salted baked wheat flour filled with sattu and spices, served with ghee and chokha.

records.name: Sattu Sharbat
records.claim: Bihar Tourism describes sattu sharbat as a savory or sweet drink made with sattu, water and seasonings and identifies it as a Bihari drink.

records.name: Thekua
records.claim: Bihar Tourism describes thekua as a traditional Bihari deep-fried sweet made with whole wheat flour, ghee and jaggery and offered as prasad during Chhath Puja.

records.name: Khichdi
records.claim: Bihar Tourism describes khichdi as a common Bihari food with rice, lentils and accompaniments such as aloo chokha; it also records its association with Makar Sankranti and festive prasad.

records.name: Champaran Meat / Ahuna
records.claim: Bihar Tourism identifies Champaran meat, also called Ahuna, handi meat or batlohi, as rooted in Champaran and cooked in a sealed earthen pot.

records.name: Dal Pittha
records.claim: Bihar Tourism describes Bihari dal pittha as a rice-flour dumpling with spiced lentil filling and identifies pittha as an authentic Bihari preparation.

records.name: Dahi Chuda
records.claim: Bihar Tourism records dahi chuda as a no-cook dish of flattened rice, yogurt and jaggery and links it to Makar Sankranti, often alongside tilkut.

records.name: Tilkut
records.claim: Bihar Tourism describes tilkut as a winter sweet made from pounded sesame and sugar or jaggery and associated with Makar Sankranti.

records.name: Maner Laddoo
records.claim: Bihar Tourism specifically highlights laddoo from Maner, about 30 km west of Patna, as a famous Bihari sweet.

records.name: Laung Lata
records.claim: Bihar Tourism identifies laung lata as a Bihari regional sweet made with a flour shell, mava and nuts and sealed with clove.
